newsitem.title: GREECE: Greek stocks stay on uptrend, seen climbing further.
newsitem.headline: Greek stocks stay on uptrend, seen climbing further.

text.p: Greek shares raced ahead on Monday in active trading in response to continuing euphoria after strong earnings growth posted by blue chip banking stocks, brokers said.

"Investors feel vindicated for their stock picks following the release of upbeat interim results by National Bank and Alpha Credit last week which raised hopes for similar performance by other banks," said Yiannis Kalogerakis, broker at ABN AMRO-Axias Securities.
Along with efforts to step up privatisations in the credit sector, strong earnings growth has helped banks take centre stage in investors' interest and will prop the broader market higher, he added.
But he said investors should keep a wary eye on the breakdown of banks' revenue sources.
"Banks' windfall gains are mostly a result of portfolio gains due to falling interest rates and rising stock prices rather than operating profits," Kalogerakis said.
Turnover was on the rise again following a period of subdued trading activity.

"There is increased interest from both retail and institutional investors as stocks are awakened from their summer lethargy and conditions bring back to mind the early stages of this year's rally," Kalogerakis said.
Stock prices will stay on an uptrend during August before new facts come into play," he added.
The Athens general index added 1.38 percent or 22.05 points to 1,623.44 from Friday's 1,601.39 close with banks leading the market with a 2.07 percent climb.
Turnover was boosted to 18.9 billion drachmas on volume of 3.7 million shares by active block trading.

It included two blocks of 76,000 shares of NIBID which changed hands at 16,970/17,055 drachmas, National Mortgage Bank, 2x 77,000 shares traded at 17,500/90, Euromedica, 200,000 shares at 1,020, and Hellenic Biscuits, 99,050 shares at 3,020 drachmas.
Advancers beat decliners 126 to 82 with 26 shares unchanged on 234 traded.
OTE telecom Global Depository Shares (GDS) were quoted on London's SEAQ International market at $10.6-$11.0. Two GDSs make up one share of OTE.
The Merrill Lynch call spread warrant on OTE with a strike price of 3,800 drachmas, capped at 5,000 drachmas, was quoted at 1,125-1,155 drachmas.

The recently launched second Merrill Lynch call spread warrant on OTE with a strike price of 6,800 drachmas, capped at 10,000 drachmas, was quoted at 1,093-1,153 drachmas. The warrants expire December 16, 1998. Shares of the underlying stock closed unchanged at 6,380 drachmas.
The Merrill Lynch American call warrant on a basket of 23 Greek equities that are part of the Athens general index was quoted at 673.04-716.01 drachmas. The warrants expire January 9 1998.

The ING Baring Financial Products American style call warrant based on a basket of six bank stocks was quoted at $75.66-$78.52. The strike price is set at $99.60 and the warrants expire October 8, 1997.

The ING Baring Financial Products American-style call warrant on a basket of six blue-chips denominated in drachmas was quoted at 3,762-3,988 drachmas. The strike price is set at 10,000 drachmas and the warrants expire on February 2, 1998.
The ING Baring American-style second call warrant on a basket of six bank stocks was quoted at $13.76 bid/no offer. The strike price is set at $110.0 and the warrants expire April 9 1998.

The recently launched ING Baring American-style, drachma- denominated call warrant on the bourse's benchmark index was quoted at 253-286 drachmas. The strike price is set at 1,639 points and the warrants expire May 14 1998.
